insight: A little recent rain (~3 mm) may be carrying some runoff to the shoreline — a modest upward pressure on bacteria. The model's main signals right now: high tide level is raising risk — a high tide can mobilize bacteria held in wet sand and push the waterline toward outfalls; recent rainfall is raising risk by washing bacteria-laden runoff into the surf; and hours since high tide is lowering risk — the timing relative to high tide affects how concentrated bacteria are at the shoreline. The last lab sample (5 MPN/100mL) is now 8 days old — beaches are sampled about weekly, so a reading this stale carries little weight, and this estimate leans on current conditions. It's a naturally clean, well-flushed open-coast beach (unsafe only ~3% of the time), so outside of storms it's reliably safe.

Recent rain (~13 mm over the past few days) is washing urban runoff into the surf — the single biggest cause of beach contamination — especially near storm drains and creek mouths.
